title: Oshawa killer had violent history
subtitle: The knife-wielding man who executed a fatal attack on an Oshawa family had a history of violence and spent much of the last decade in and out of courtrooms.
article: The knife-wielding man who executed a fatal attack on an Oshawa family had a history of violence and spent much of the last decade in and out of courtrooms.

Gino Petralia, 47, had been charged with assault on three separate occasions, two in 2004 and one in 1998. He has also faced charges of impaired driving, failure to comply and fail to appear. Most recently, he was arrested in January for causing a disturbance in a public place. He had been scheduled to appear in Oshawa court later this month.
On Saturday, a Durham police officer shot Petralia dead, after the man went on a murderous rampage in a south Oshawa townhouse.

It was around dusk. Leslie and Rick Kelly were celebrating 11-year-old Brandon's birthday, when Petralia stormed the home and began slashing, reportedly attacking the couple's youngest children first. Family friends said 3-year-old Nathan and 5-year-old Riley were playing downstairs.

When the Kellys heard screams, they ran to the ground floor. Leslie jumped in front of her husband as the attacker swung. Rick threw himself in front of the children, forcing Petralia out the door. The man ran to a nearby apartment.

Even though she was mortally wounded, Leslie, 26, was able to dial 911. Nathan is still fighting for his life; 5-year-old Riley remains in hospital with serious injuries. Rick underwent surgery and was also recovering in hospital yesterday.

The province's Special Investigations Unit is probing the case, so Durham police could offer few details. But it is believed the Kellys had recently gained custody of Petralia's son, Steven, 13, who is Rick's half-brother. Steven, Brandon and a 12-year-old cousin were in the house, but were not injured.

At his home yesterday, Petralia's uncle Luigi asked for privacy. "We're trying to stay neutral," he said, visibly shaken. For about eight years, Petralia lived just two doors down with his mother, Luigi's sister. Neighbours said the large family is warm and friendly, but that Petralia was always strange.
"Sometimes we'd see him shovelling the driveway, throwing the snow on the road. Then when he was done, he'd put it back. Stuff like that," said one neighbour.
Petralia's mother did not come to the door yesterday. A floral delivery came about 1 p.m. A neighbour offered to hold the flowers.
